circulars.title: The Constitution of India (Comprehensive Text with Preamble & Amendments)
circulars.circularNumber: Supreme Lex of Bharat • Ministry of Law & Justice Codification
circulars.issuingAuthority: Constituent Assembly of India / Ministry of Law and Justice, Govt. of India
circulars.summary: The supreme organic law and constitutional foundation of the Republic of Bharat. Enshrines sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic principles, fundamental rights, directive principles of state policy, fundamental duties, and the constitutional architecture of legislative, executive, and judicial governance.
keyProvisions: Preamble: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic securing Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity and Integrity of the Nation.
Part III (Articles 12-35): Fundamental Rights including Right to Equality (Art. 14), Protection of Personal Liberty (Art. 21), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art. 32).
Part IV (Articles 36-51): Directive Principles of State Policy including Article 44 directing the State to secure a Uniform Civil Code.
Part IV-A (Article 51A): Fundamental Duties of every citizen to cherish constitutional ideals and civilizational heritage.
Part XVIII (Articles 352-360) & Part XX (Article 368): Constitutional Amendment mechanisms and Emergency Powers.
circulars.sourceName: Ministry of Law & Justice, Legislative Dept (legislative.gov.in)

circulars.title: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023
circulars.circularNumber: Act No. 45 of 2023 • Gazette of India Ext. Part II-Sec 1
circulars.issuingAuthority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India
circulars.summary: Consolidates and modernizes the substantive criminal law of Bharat, completely replacing the colonial Indian Penal Code, 1860. Introduces community service as a progressive restorative penal sanction, strengthens protections for women and minors, and establishes precise definitions for organized crime, mob violence, and economic sabotage.
keyProvisions: Section 4: Recognizes community service as an official penal sanction for minor offences to promote restorative rehabilitation.
Sections 63-79: Overhauled framework for crimes against women and children with severe statutory minimum sentencing.
Section 69: Criminalizes sexual relations procured through deceitful promises of marriage or employment.
Section 111: Defines and penalizes Organized Crime syndicates, illicit trafficking, and systemic extortion.
Section 113: Statutory definitions and stringent penalties for Terrorist Acts and sovereign endangerment.
circulars.sourceName: e-Gazette of India & Ministry of Home Affairs (mha.gov.in / egazette.gov.in)

circulars.title: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023
circulars.circularNumber: Act No. 46 of 2023 • Gazette of India Ext. Part II-Sec 1
circulars.issuingAuthority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India
circulars.summary: Replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973. Mandates contemporary digital evidence handling, electronic first information reports (e-FIR), mandatory forensic videography during searches and seizures, time-bound trial schedules, and summary trials for petty matters.
keyProvisions: Section 173: Formal statutory establishment of electronic FIRs (e-FIR) and Zero FIR jurisdiction across all police stations.
Section 176(3): Mandatory forensic expert presence and videographic evidence capture at scenes of serious offences (punishable by 7+ years).
Section 258: Streamlined plea-bargaining processes to resolve judicial backlogs within institutional deadlines.
Section 530: Statutory recognition of electronic summons, virtual witness depositions, and digital trial proceedings.
circulars.sourceName: e-Gazette of India & Ministry of Home Affairs (mha.gov.in / egazette.gov.in)
circulars.contentPreview:
An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Criminal Procedure.
Be it enacted by Parliament in the Seventy-fourth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

CHAPTER I: PRELIMINARY
1. (1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
(2) It shall come into force on the 1st day of July, 2024.

Section 173. Information in cognizable cases.—
(1) Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer in charge of a police station...

circulars.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP Act), 2023
circulars.circularNumber: Act No. 22 of 2023 • Ministry of Electronics & IT (MeitY)
circulars.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Govt. of India
circulars.summary: Establishes a statutory framework for processing digital personal data respecting individual autonomy and lawful national public interests. Defines obligations of Data Fiduciaries, statutory consent notices, rights of Data Principals, protections for children, and the formation of the Data Protection Board of India.
keyProvisions: Section 4: Grounds for processing personal data on the basis of informed consent or legitimate lawful uses.
Section 6: Clear, itemized consent notices in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
Section 9: Mandatory additional obligations regarding children's personal data and prohibition of tracking.
Section 18: Constitution and powers of the Data Protection Board of India for inquiry and penalty adjudications.
circulars.contentPreview:
An Act to provide for the processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognises both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process such personal data for lawful purposes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

Section 4. Grounds for processing personal data.—
(1) A person may process the personal data of a Data Principal only—
(a) for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given her consent; or
(b) for certain legitimate uses as specified in section 7.

circulars.title: Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Model Legislative Framework & Harmonized Civil Guidelines
circulars.issuingAuthority: Bharat Collective Legal Secretariat & Law Commission Consultative Bench
circulars.summary: A civilizational model legal framework prepared under Article 44 of the Constitution of India. Establishes uniform civic standards for marriage solemnization and mandatory registration, gender-equal inheritance and succession laws, equitable maintenance during divorce, and secular protection of women and orphaned minors.
keyProvisions: Clause 2: Secular definitions of civil marriage, domestic cohabitation, legal guardianship, and intestate succession.
Clause 5: Universal mandatory registration of marriages and civil partnerships to eliminate child marriage and coercive unions.
Clause 8: Absolute gender parity in ancestral and self-acquired property inheritance, regardless of customary exclusions.
Clause 14: Objective, judicial formula-based alimony and child support criteria prioritizing custodial welfare.
circulars.sourceName: Bharat Collective Consultative Bench (Article 44 Mandate Reference)
circulars.contentPreview:
BHARAT COLLECTIVE FOUNDATION: MODEL BILL ON UNIFORM CIVIL JURISPRUDENCE
Pursuant to Article 44 of the Constitution of India:

1. Short Title and Commencement:
(1) This Act may be cited as the Uniform Civil Code (Model Harmonization) Framework, 2024.
(2) It shall apply to all citizens within the territory of India irrespective of religious denomination.

2. Equal Rights in Succession:
Every daughter and son shall inherit an equal and indivisible share in ancestral and parental estate upon intestate demise, superseding customary discriminations.

circulars.title: The Right to Information Act (RTI Act), 2005 & Compendium of DoPT Circulars
circulars.circularNumber: Act No. 22 of 2005 • Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
circulars.issuingAuthority: Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), Govt. of India
circulars.summary: Comprehensive statutory guide to India's freedom of information framework. Details procedural rules for public information requests, designated Public Information Officers (PIOs), first and second appellate remedies, suo motu disclosures under Section 4, and statutory exemption boundaries.
keyProvisions: Section 3: Affirmation that all citizens shall have the right to information subject to the provisions of this Act.
Section 4: Mandatory proactive public disclosure by all public authorities via digital portals.
Section 7: 30-day strict compliance deadline (48 hours where life or liberty is involved) for providing requested records.
Section 8: Exemption grounds including national security, sovereignty, judicial contempt, and fiduciary privilege.
circulars.sourceName: Department of Personnel and Training, Govt. of India (rti.gov.in)
circulars.contentPreview:
An Act to provide for setting out the practical regime of right to information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority...

Section 3. Right to information.—Subject to the provisions of this Act, all citizens shall have the right to information.

circulars.title: Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam)
circulars.circularNumber: Act No. 34 of 2023 • Ministry of Law & Justice Gazette
circulars.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Law and Justice (Legislative Department), Govt. of India
circulars.summary: Historic constitutional amendment reserving one-third (33%) of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha (House of the People), State Legislative Assemblies, and the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, revolutionizing women-led democratic governance.
keyProvisions: Insertion of Article 330A: 33% reservation for women in seats allocated to Scheduled Castes and general constituencies in the Lok Sabha.
Insertion of Article 332A: 33% mandatory reservation for women in all State Legislative Assemblies across Bharat.
Insertion of Article 334A: Implementation linked with the first delimitation exercise and effective for a fifteen-year sunset period.
circulars.sourceName: Ministry of Law & Justice, Legislative Dept (legislative.gov.in)
circulars.contentPreview:
THE CONSTITUTION (ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
[28th September, 2023.]
An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.
BE it enacted by Parliament in the Seventy-fourth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023.
2. Insertion of new article 330A.—After article 330 of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—
"330A. (1) Seats shall be reserved for women in the House of the People..."

circulars.title: Supreme Court Standard Operating Procedure: Virtual Court Proceedings & Digital Accessibility
circulars.issuingAuthority: Registry of the Supreme Court of India & e-Committee
circulars.summary: Comprehensive practice directives and standard operating procedures (SOP) governing hybrid judicial hearings, electronic filing (e-Filing 3.0), digital evidence submission guidelines, and live-streaming protocols for Constitutional and larger bench hearings.
keyProvisions: Directive 1: Universal right of appearing counsels, litigants-in-person, and media correspondents to attend via hybrid video conferencing.
Directive 4: Standardized digital document indexing, OCR text-searchable PDF submission, and electronic book-marking.
Directive 7: Live-streaming protocols preserving open justice while protecting personal dignity in sensitive matrimonial and POCSO hearings.
circulars.sourceName: Supreme Court of India, Registry & e-Committee (sci.gov.in)
circulars.contentPreview:
SUPREME COURT OF INDIA: E-COMMITTEE STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP)
Subject: Seamless Conduct of Hybrid Hearings and Digital Case Management across Constitutional Benches.

1. Universal Hybrid Accessibility:
No court shall insist on physical-only appearances where counsel or party-in-person exercises the option to appear through authorized high-definition video conferencing platform.
